claim: [FACTS] GaussiAnimate achieves significant reanimation performance improvements, with 17.3% PSNR gains over Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) and 21.7% over Bag-of-Bones (BoB), while its Partwise Motion Matching (PartMM) algorithm shows 48.4% RMSE improvement over robust LBS.

[FACTS] ETCH-X delivers substantial performance improvements in expressive body fitting, including an 80.8% MPJPE-All improvement and 80.5% V2V-All improvement on unseen BEDLAM2.0 data, and 33.0% MPJPE-All on 4D-Dress.

[FACTS] NUMINA improves counting accuracy in text-to-video diffusion models by up to 7.4% on Wan2.1-1.3B models, and by 4.9% and 5.5% on 5B and 14B models respectively, while also enhancing CLIP alignment and maintaining temporal consistency.

[TECHNICAL] GaussiAnimate introduces a "Skelebones" rigging system that compresses temporally-consistent deformable Gaussians into free-form bones, extracts a Mean Curvature Skeleton, and binds them via non-parametric Partwise Motion Matching to capture non-rigid deformations and enable intuitive control of 4D shapes.

[TECHNICAL] ETCH-X upgrades its predecessor by leveraging a tightness-aware fitting paradigm to 'undress' clothing dynamics, extending expressiveness with SMPL-X, and replacing sparse markers with implicit dense correspondences ('dense fit'), enabling scalable training on composable datasets like CLOTH3D, AMASS, and InterHand2.6M.

[TECHNICAL] NUMINA is a training-free 'identify-then-guide' framework for text-to-video diffusion models that identifies prompt-layout inconsistencies by selecting discriminative self- and cross-attention heads to derive a countable latent layout, then refines and modulates cross-attention for guided regeneration.

[CONTEXT] These advancements in 4D shape animation, expressive human body fitting, and numerically accurate text-to-video generation are crucial for enhancing realism and control in various applications such as animation, virtual reality, gaming, and the creation of digital humans.

[RESEARCH] GaussiAnimate's Partwise Motion Matching algorithm demonstrates strong generalization capabilities, outperforming GRU- and MLP-based learning methods by over 20%, particularly in low-data regimes (~1000 frames).

[FACTS] A significant percentage of employees, especially Gen Z, admit to sabotaging their company's AI strategy. A report found 29% of all employees and 44% of Gen Z workers actively undermine AI initiatives.

[FACTS] The primary motivation for AI sabotage is fear of job loss, with 30% of saboteurs citing concerns that AI will take their job. This 'Fear Of Becoming Obsolete' (FOBO) is widespread, with 4 out of 10 workers generally fearing AI could replace them.

[TECHNICAL] Sabotage methods include entering proprietary company information into public AI tools, using unapproved AI tools, outright refusal to use AI, tampering with performance reviews, and intentionally generating low-output work to make AI appear ineffective.

[CONTEXT] Despite sabotage efforts, a large percentage of Gen Z workers (88%) also actively use AI to perform their jobs, overcome 'task paralysis,' and improve efficiency, indicating a dual perception of AI as both a threat and a valuable productivity tool.

[CONTEXT] Employee resistance to AI poses a significant threat to companies, with 76% of C-suite executives viewing it as a serious risk. Paradoxically, 60% of executives are considering cutting employees who refuse to adopt AI, making resistors more vulnerable to layoffs.

[RESEARCH] Warnings from AI leaders like Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman suggest AI could automate a significant portion of entry-level white-collar jobs (up to half or even all within 18 months), fueling worker anxieties.

[CONTEXT] Beyond job loss, other factors contributing to AI resistance include concerns about security risks (28%), diminished creativity or value (26%), poorly executed company AI strategy (26%), distrust of AI accuracy, environmental impact, and the risk of over-reliance.
